reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the core mechanistic premises linking lattice distortion to entropy-driven stabilization, sluggish diffusion, or property optimization. E1 shows clustering at low Al, E2 discusses fcc vs. hcp properties without addressing Al-induced distortion, and E3 only reports a single-phase structure and mechanical properties for one composition, offering no comparative or mechanistic insight.
premises: Phase stability is governed by a balance between configurational entropy and lattice distortion energy from Al atomic size mismatch.
Moderate Al additions increase lattice distortion, which enhances configurational entropy's stabilizing effect on a disordered single phase.
This distorted lattice slows atomic diffusion, enhancing high-temperature strength, radiation tolerance, and environmental resistance.
Excessive lattice distortion promotes local chemical ordering or precipitation, degrading properties.
An optimal Al concentration window exists where single-phase stability and property balance are maximized.
